correctness.rationale: For any deterministic initial unit coin, Haar invariance makes the first coin a uniform complex-sphere vector, with fourth moments 2/[d(d+1)] and 1/[d(d+1)]. Explicit second-step amplitudes at e_a XOR e_b yield a diagonal purity contribution (d+3)/(d+1)^2. For b!=b', two and only two unordered coordinate-flip histories yield matching terminal vertices, and phase symmetry removes their cross term. The disjoint-row/column Haar unitary moment 1/(d^2-1) yields off-diagonal 2/(d+1)^2. Their sum is (d+5)/(d+1)^2; subtraction gives the dimension-three crossover and the exact contrast with the averaged coin I/d. No limit or computation beyond finite-dimensional Haar integration is needed. The packaged verify.py independently recomputes amplitudes and 36,000 coin samples with 40 passed assertion groups; Monte Carlo is corroboration, not proof. The d=1 singular moment case is excluded.

originality.rationale: Quillen (2026) introduces exactly this hypercube walk and proves linear averaged-channel depolarization, not the nonlinear mean of realized reduced-coin purity. Full text of the OA 15-page article was inspected at the model and averaged-channel sections and searched for purity and entanglement. Vieira et al. (2013) investigate long-time two-state disordered-coin entanglement on a line; Fang et al. (2023) optimize finite deterministic coin sequences in a different two-state walk. Neither supplies the d-dimensional Haar contraction or sign reversal. Searches for the formulas, the parameter threshold, and random coin-purity equivalents gave no equivalent identified theorem. Established Weingarten calculus is acknowledged as an underlying tool; implicit coverage by uninspected general higher-moment random-circuit results remains possible. The claim is a model-specific explicit nonlinear crossover, not the discovery of general Haar integration.
residual_risks: Broader random-quantum-circuit fourth-moment or tensor-network results may implicitly subsume the two-step formula.
The survey of published literature is bounded; novelty has not been independently certified.
The physical importance of the exact d=3 early-time crossover may depend on whether this same effect persists in related graph or noise ensembles, which is unproved.

value.rationale: Averaged-channel depolarization cannot determine the nonlinear entanglement of the underlying pure stochastic trajectories. The first and second steps are structurally distinguished because the second is the first moment when opposite orderings of coordinate flips interfere at equal vertices. The sharp d=3 direction reversal, dependence only on graph degree and exact purity-versus-depolarization gap provide a natural diagnostic of entanglement growth and graph-induced interference, not an arbitrary numerical slice. The all-dimensional finite-time result is meaningful without a larger theorem; extension to later times and other graph shifts remains open.
